title: Filtered colimits of smooth algebras and products
statement: Let $R_1\to\Lambda_1$ and $R_2\to\Lambda_2$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings such that, for $i=1,2$, $\Lambda_i$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R_i$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. Then $\Lambda_1\times\Lambda_2$, an $R_1\times R_2$-algebra via the product map $(r_1,r_2)\mapsto(\varphi_1(r_1),\varphi_2(r_2))$, is a filtered colimit of smooth $R_1\times R_2$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. (Stacks states this inside Situation 07F2, i.e. for regular maps $R_i\to\Lambda_i$ of Noetherian rings; its hint, 'a product of filtered colimits is a filtered colimit', does not use these hypotheses, and the statement here omits them.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F3 (lemma-product, line 1926), stated in Situation Tag 07F2; proof 'Omitted. Hint: A product of filtered colimits is a filtered colimit.'

proof.text: *Step 1 (the data and the product index category).* By [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras] there are a small filtered category $I$, a functor $i\mapsto A_i$ from $I$ to commutative $R_1$-algebras (transition maps $A_a:A_i\to A_{i'}$ for $a:i\to i'$) with every $A_i$ smooth over $R_1$, and $R_1$-algebra maps $\iota_i:A_i\to\Lambda_1$ making $(\Lambda_1,(\iota_i))$ a colimit in commutative $R_1$-algebras; likewise a small filtered $J$, smooth $R_2$-algebras $B_j$ with transition maps $B_b$, and a colimit cocone $(\Lambda_2,(\kappa_j))$ in commutative $R_2$-algebras. The product category $I\times J$ (objects $(i,j)$, morphisms $(a,b):(i,j)\to(i',j')$ with componentwise composition) is small and filtered in the sense of Stacks 002V: it has an object $(i_0,j_0)$ as $I$, $J$ are nonempty; for $(i,j)$, $(i',j')$ choose $a:i\to i''$, $a':i'\to i''$ in $I$ and $b:j\to j''$, $b':j'\to j''$ in $J$, so $(a,b)$, $(a',b')$ go to $(i'',j'')$; for parallel arrows $(a,b),(a',b'):(i,j)\to(i',j')$ choose $c:i'\to i''$ with $ca=ca'$ and $d:j'\to j''$ with $db=db'$, then $(c,d)(a,b)=(c,d)(a',b')$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07F3 (lemma-product, line 1926), proof 'Omitted. Hint: A product of filtered colimits is a filtered colimit', written out

proof.text: *Step 2 (a diagram of smooth $R_1\times R_2$-algebras).* Put $R=R_1\times R_2$ and $D(i,j)=A_i\times B_j$, an $R$-algebra via $(r_1,r_2)\mapsto(r_1\cdot1,r_2\cdot1)$, and $D(a,b)=A_a\times B_b:(x,y)\mapsto(A_a(x),B_b(y))$; this is a ring homomorphism compatible with the structure maps (each component is), and $D$ preserves identities and composition because $i\mapsto A_i$ and $j\mapsto B_j$ do; so $D$ is a functor from $I\times J$ to commutative $R$-algebras. Since $R_1\to A_i$ and $R_2\to B_j$ are smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $R=R_1\times R_2\to A_i\times B_j$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-product-ring].

source.place: Lemma Tag 07F3 (lemma-product, line 1926), proof 'Omitted. Hint: A product of filtered colimits is a filtered colimit', written out

proof.text: *Step 3 (the cocone).* Make $\Lambda_1\times\Lambda_2$ an $R$-algebra by the product of the structure maps (the algebra structure of the statement). The maps $\theta_{(i,j)}=\iota_i\times\kappa_j:A_i\times B_j\to\Lambda_1\times\Lambda_2$ are $R$-algebra homomorphisms, and for $(a,b):(i,j)\to(i',j')$ we have $\theta_{(i',j')}\circ D(a,b)=(\iota_{i'}A_a)\times(\kappa_{j'}B_b)=\iota_i\times\kappa_j=\theta_{(i,j)}$, so $(\Lambda_1\times\Lambda_2,(\theta_{(i,j)}))$ is a cocone on $D$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Lemma Tag 07F3 (lemma-product, line 1926), proof 'Omitted. Hint: A product of filtered colimits is a filtered colimit', written out

proof.text: *Step 4 (the colimit, checked on underlying types).* Forgetting a filtered colimit of commutative R-algebras to commutative rings preserves its universal property, even when the base has a smaller universe: for any ring cocone choose an index i, give its apex the algebra map obtained by composing the structure map at i with the cocone leg, and use common upper objects to show every other leg commutes with that map. Lift the ring cocone to an algebra cocone and apply the original colimit universal property. Forgetting filtered ring colimits to types preserves them (Mathlib's Ring.FilteredColimits). Thus each coordinate colimit is jointly surjective, and equality of two elements represented at the same stage holds at a later stage (Types.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit and Types.FilteredColimit.isColimit_eq_iff'). For the product cocone, represent the first and second coordinates at i and j; their pair represents the element at (i,j). If two pairs at (i,j) have equal images, find f:i→k and g:j→l witnessing the respective coordinate equalities; the arrow (f,g) witnesses equality in the product diagram. The recognition lemma Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' proves this underlying type cocone colimiting. To recover the algebra colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], first reflect through the ring forgetful functor (which preserves these colimits and reflects isomorphisms); then lift the resulting universal ring map to an algebra map by checking its structure-map compatibility on the leg at any index. Existence, factorization and uniqueness follow from the ring universal property. This uses no idempotent decomposition of the destination.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07F3 (lemma-product, line 1926), proof 'Omitted. Hint: A product of filtered colimits is a filtered colimit', written out

proof.text: *Step 5 (conclusion).* $I\times J$ is a small filtered category (Step 1), $D$ is a functor from it to commutative $R_1\times R_2$-algebras with every $D(i,j)$ smooth over $R_1\times R_2$ (Step 2), and $(\Lambda_1\times\Lambda_2,(\theta_{(i,j)}))$ is a colimit of $D$ in commutative $R_1\times R_2$-algebras (Steps 3, 4); by [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras], $\Lambda_1\times\Lambda_2$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R_1\times R_2$-algebras.

Statement and stmt_deps kept (the statement already omits the Noetherian/regular hypotheses of Situation 07F2, which the hint does not use; the citer lem-weil-pbc-popescu-reduce-to-field Step 5 applies it to iterated products K_1 x ... x K_s, which are not fields, so the general form is the one needed). Proof is by agent (Stacks omits it). New node: lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-product-ring (unsplit, no Mathlib match; Stacks 0GIF states only the product over one base R).
